breaking_news.headline: Jennifer Welch isn't holding back on Trump, Democrats or political division
breaking_news.summary: The podcaster talks to Leila Fadel about her new book, her evolving politics and what it means to build a future with people whose views she strongly opposes.

breaking_news.headline: Here's the latest sticker shock: Borrowing for a mortgage -- or a car
breaking_news.summary: It's not just mortgages being at their highest level in almost three years — but the cost of loans for cars and higher education are among the borrowing costs affected, too.

breaking_news.headline: Who will win the 2026 Nobel Prize in economics?
breaking_news.summary: A thinly traded prediction market offers a starting point. We explore potential winners and the big ideas that could earn them economics' biggest prize.

breaking_news.headline: Why Trump just loosened the rules on 'dyed diesel' — normally a farm fuel
breaking_news.summary: Trump is temporarily allowing this fuel to be used on highways, although it's typically just for off-road farm and construction vehicles. Could that lower the price of diesel?

breaking_news.headline: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
breaking_news.summary: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

breaking_news.headline: OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns
breaking_news.summary: The company says Russian operatives used its AI chatbot to update their bosses, shedding light on influence campaigns previously not attributed to Russia.

breaking_news.headline: Why American investors love European defense startups
breaking_news.summary: As European defense spending takes off, just about half of the funding in Europe's defense tech industry is coming from American investors this year. One reason why: European investment firms have restrictions on how they can invest.

breaking_news.headline: How the oil industry is preparing for Hurricane Isaias
breaking_news.summary: Hurricane Isaias is this season's first Atlantic hurricane, and is on a path to hit the northern Gulf Coast. How is the oil industry preparing?

breaking_news.headline: US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
breaking_news.summary: Oscar Belgal, the 28-year-old man, survived the shooting and is now being held at a detention facility outside of New York, officials said.

breaking_news.headline: Ethiopia warns Eritrea it will defend itself after troops cross border
breaking_news.summary: Truckloads of Eritrean soldiers have been seen driving into Ethiopia, which has reportedly responded with drone strikes.

breaking_news.headline: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
breaking_news.summary: The left-wing candidate won a narrow victory in a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, exit polls show.

breaking_news.headline: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
breaking_news.summary: The heist at the Florence-based winery is believed to be one of the largest thefts of its kind in Italy.

breaking_news.headline: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
breaking_news.summary: Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the tech firm admits customers may experience disruption to digital services due to the attacks.

breaking_news.headline: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
breaking_news.summary: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

breaking_news.headline: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
breaking_news.summary: Pillay is recognised for her "efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee says.

breaking_news.headline: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
breaking_news.summary: Several member states of the international tribunal, including the UK, say they "strongly disagree" with the sanctions.

breaking_news.headline: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for 'prioritising safety'
breaking_news.summary: The AI firm instead claims the researchers were fired for mishandling sensitive information.

breaking_news.headline: 'Add me on WhatsApp' scam calls to be investigated
breaking_news.summary: The UK's data watchdog is investigating a spike in complaints about "robo calls" that appear to lead to a recruitment scam.

breaking_news.headline: Why are more roofs not made of solar tiles?
breaking_news.summary: Solar tiles were touted as an attractive alternative to solar panels - why have they not taken off?

breaking_news.headline: Anthropic bans users from being 'cruel' to its AI systems
breaking_news.summary: The firm said users can no longer engage in "sustained and needless" abusive behaviour towards the tech.
